The data don't settle the direction on their own. Residual_u10m and Residual_heat_flux are only weakly correlated (Pearson 0.12, Spearman 0.11). Nonlinear fits in both directions explain very little (R² about 0.02) and look about equally good, so there is no statistical asymmetry to read a direction from.

I'm going with the physics. Near-surface wind drives turbulent heat exchange between the surface and the atmosphere, so wind affecting heat flux is far more plausible than the reverse. That is a judgement from domain knowledge, not something the data confirmed.

ANSWER: A
